what: The Avengers undo Thanos's snap with a time heist, and it costs them. Tony Stark dies using the Stones. Steve Rogers goes back in time to live the life he missed with Peggy, then returns as an old man and hands the shield to Sam Wilson. Thor gives up the throne and flies off with the Guardians.
why: The people who held the MCU together are gone or retired. No new Avengers team forms after this.
lead: The heist leaves one loose end. In 2012, a Loki grabs the Tesseract and disappears. That small slip is what drags the TVA, and the whole multiverse, into the story.

what: That runaway Loki gets arrested by the TVA, an agency that deletes any timeline that drifts from the one allowed “Sacred Timeline.” The man behind it is He Who Remains, a Kang variant who won a war against his own variants and built the TVA so it could never happen again. Sylvie kills him, and timelines start branching everywhere. In season 2 the machine holding them is failing, so Loki takes its place and holds every branch together himself, like a living tree.
why: Time is no longer locked to one path. The multiverse is wide open and growing, and Loki is what keeps it from falling apart.
lead: That's why Loki's return in Doomsday is a big deal. The man holding all those realities together is back in the middle of the fight.

w: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
what: Strange lands on Earth-838 and meets its Illuminati. They explain that their own Strange caused an incursion, which is when two universes run into each other and destroy each other. In the mid-credits scene, Clea pulls our Strange through a portal and tells him he has caused one too.
why: This is the first time the MCU names the real danger of an open multiverse. Realities aren't just side doors anymore. They can collide.
lead: Incursions are the ticking clock of this whole saga. In the comics, they lead straight into Secret Wars, and that's the film that comes right after Doomsday.

what: Deadpool's world, the universe of the old Fox X-Men films that the TVA calls Earth-10005, is fading away. Its “anchor being” was Logan, and he died in Logan (2017). Deadpool recruits a Wolverine variant from another world, they save the day, and that Wolverine stays as the new anchor.
why: The Fox films are no longer a separate franchise. They're officially a real place in the MCU multiverse, and the TVA knows it exists.
lead: That's the universe Doomsday's X-Men come from: Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen, James Marsden, Rebecca Romijn, Alan Cumming, Kelsey Grammer and Channing Tatum.

what: Kang was supposed to be the big bad. Quantumania introduced him and ended on a whole Council of Kangs. After Jonathan Majors was convicted at the end of 2023, Marvel let him go. Kevin Feige has said they'd already started to feel Kang wasn't big enough to be the next Thanos. At San Diego Comic-Con in July 2024, Avengers: The Kang Dynasty became Avengers: Doomsday, and Robert Downey Jr. pulled off a mask as Doctor Doom.
why: Doom is often called Marvel's greatest villain, and the studio could only use him after Disney bought Fox. He's now the villain of both Doomsday and Secret Wars.
lead: Doom steps into the multiverse-sized threat Kang was built for, but he's a very different kind of villain. Read the next panel to see how he's been set up.

w: Thunderbolts* · The Fantastic Four: First Steps
what: Thunderbolts* ends with Valentina selling Yelena's crew of misfits to the world as the New Avengers. Its last post-credits scene shows an “extradimensional” ship with the Fantastic Four's logo entering Earth's orbit. First Steps is set on Earth-828, where the Fantastic Four stop Galactus, who wanted baby Franklin for his huge power. In the mid-credits scene, four years later, Doctor Doom is in the Baxter Building talking to Franklin. Then a title card: “The Fantastic Four will return in Avengers: Doomsday.”
why: Now there are two hero teams, two worlds and one villain who can clearly cross between them. Feige has teased that the ship in Thunderbolts* might not be the same one the Fantastic Four flew.
lead: The Fantastic Four are heading for our universe, and Doom has already found their son. That's the setup Doomsday opens on.

what: Marvel's official pitch is that heroes from three separate universes end up on a collision course against a threat unlike any before. Feige told Empire the Avengers reassemble for the first time since Endgame, this time led by Sam Wilson. He also shut down the Tony Stark theory: Doom isn't a variant of Tony, “He's Victor Von Doom.” Joe Russo says Doom looking like Tony will all make sense when you see the film.
why: Everything since Endgame lands here: the open multiverse, the incursions, the Fox X-Men, the Fantastic Four and Doom.
lead: It's part one of two. The Russos say Doomsday and Secret Wars (Dec 17, 2027) tell one story together, connected like Infinity War and Endgame were, but not in exactly the same way.
